items.title: Spec: agent setup (codebase map, database safety, iteration commands)
items.body:
## Problem Statement

Coding agents working on slopstagram waste time and put the maintainer's data at risk.

- **No map.** Agents re-discover the layout and the two pipelines in every session, because AGENTS.md lists rules but no map.
- **Damage to the live database.** One agent session already let a dev server apply pending migrations to it (recorded in the archived sticker refactoring post-mortem). Nothing in the setup makes that hard to repeat.
- **Worktrees start empty.** The data directory resolves from the current folder, so an agent working in a worktree has no database and no media cache.
- **Slow feedback loop.** Agents don't know the quick commands, and they run the full check, which rewrites formatting and runs everything, as their inner loop.

## Solution

AGENTS.md gains three things:

- a short codebase map: the two pipelines, one line per top-level area, and where tests go
- a database safety rule: anything that writes runs against a copy
- the quick iteration commands

The tooling backs this up:

- a snapshot command copies the live database consistently
- the migration step backs up the database before applying pending migrations
- a data directory override lets a worktree point at the main checkout's data, or a copy of it

## User Stories

1. As a coding agent, I want a codebase map in AGENTS.md, so that I find where to work without exploring.
2. As a coding agent, I want the fetch-run pipeline drawn as a call tree (script or hourly job, report creation, fetching stories, enrichment, database), so that I know how data gets in.
3. As a coding agent, I want the page pipeline drawn as a call tree (route loader, server function, page loader, repositories), so that I know how data gets out.
4. As a coding agent, I want one line per top-level area saying what belongs there and what doesn't, so that I put new code in the right place.
5. As a coding agent, I want the test naming rule in the map, so that I find a module's tests by name.
6. As a coding agent, I want the map to point to the glossary and the ADRs, so that I use the domain vocabulary and respect past decisions.
7. As the maintainer, I want the map written after the folder restructure lands, so that it doesn't describe folders that are about to move.
8. As the maintainer, I want an AGENTS.md rule that anything writing the database runs against a copy, so that agents never write my live data.
9. As a coding agent, I want one command that snapshots the live database to a working copy, so that following the rule is easy.
10. As the maintainer, I want the snapshot to be consistent while the database is in use, so that copies are never corrupt.
11. As the maintainer, I want an automatic backup before pending migrations are applied, so that a bad migration can be rolled back.
12. As the maintainer, I want no backup taken when there is nothing to migrate, so that backups don't pile up on every start.
13. As the maintainer, I want backups named by time in the existing backups folder, so that I can find the one I need.
14. As a coding agent in a worktree, I want to point the app at another data directory, so that I can work with real data without copying it by hand.
15. As a coding agent, I want the data directory override documented next to the database rule, so that I set both correctly.
16. As the maintainer, I want an optional guard that blocks starting the dev server or running migrations when no database override is set, so that the rule is enforced and not only written down.
17. As a coding agent, I want the single-test-file command in AGENTS.md, so that my inner loop takes seconds.
18. As a coding agent, I want the lint and dead-code commands in AGENTS.md, so that I can check types and unused code without running everything.
19. As a coding agent, I want AGENTS.md to say the full check rewrites formatting and belongs before committing, so that I don't run it on every change.
20. As the maintainer, I want the archived docs left out of the map, so that agents don't read stale designs.

## Implementation Decisions

- **AGENTS.md sections:**
  - a codebase map of about 30 lines: the two pipelines as call trees, one line per area, the test naming rule, pointers to the glossary and ADRs
  - database safety
  - iteration commands
- **Snapshot command:** an npm script that uses SQLite's consistent copy (VACUUM INTO) to write a working copy into the data directory.
- **Backup before migrating:** the migration helper, already used by the server plugin and by tests, checks for pending migrations. When some exist, it writes a timestamped consistent copy to the backups folder before applying them. Scripts still never migrate.
- **Data directory override:** an environment variable alongside the existing database path override. It moves the database, the media cache and the Playwright profile together.
- **Optional guard:** a Claude Code PreToolUse hook that refuses to start the dev server or run migrations unless the database path override is set. The maintainer decides whether to enable it.
- **The codebase map waits** for the folder structure spec to land.

## Testing Decisions

- One seam: the migration helper, run against a temporary file database.
  - Pending migrations produce a backup before the schema changes.
  - No pending migrations produce no backup.
  - The snapshot command produces a database that opens and holds the same rows.
- The data directory override is tested through the data path configuration: with it set, the database, cache and profile paths all resolve under it.
- Prior art: the migration tests that migrate isolated databases, and the database client tests that use an explicit database path.

## Out of Scope

- A secrets-scanning hook for file reads (decided against).
- Archiving stale docs and mapping glossary terms to code (done in #79).
- The testing strategy (#90) and the folder structure (#89).

## Further Notes

- The codebase map depends on #89.
- The AGENTS.md Testing section comes from #90.

items.title: Keep the bridge when a safety override replaces the reply
items.body:
When a custom expert's verdict maps to `override` or `short_circuit`, the V2 agent sends the fixed template on its own under the bridge's `transcript_id`. If the bridge is still being spoken:
- the chat bubble and teleprompter jump to the template, and the bridge text disappears;
- TTS sees a chunk that doesn't extend its buffer, resets, and the bridge is cut off mid-sentence.

The fix is https://github.com/c4dhi/STELLA/pull/644. It prefixes the bridge to the deterministic response, as the Response Generator already does, and speaks the template at the bridge's speed. It merges cleanly into `development`.

**Verify:** a local run in which an override fires while the bridge is speaking. The bridge must finish without being cut off, and the bubble must show bridge plus template. Unit tests alone are not enough.

— atlas

items.title: feat(safety): project-scoped override for declared form paths in the sensitive-path gate
items.body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and did not find a request for this feature.
- [x] I reviewed this request and removed credentials, tokens, private paths, hostnames, and other sensitive data.

### Problem or opportunity

The harness-wide sensitive-path gate denies agent read/edit of
`secrets/contract.yaml` and `secrets/contract-allowlist.yaml` in secret-ops
repos, but these files are pure form: record paths, property names,
generator names (`external:VAR`), key mappings — zero values. A repo lane
skill (OpenBao operator, `contract → converge → ESO → audit`) orders agents
to author contract entries, so the gate makes the repo's own documented
workflow unexecutable by agents; the only fallback is a human hand-pasting
form YAML. Related but distinct: #2349 (guard bypassable via bash — the
deny list covers only read/write/edit; my own `sed`/`grep` reads of the
same file went through, which is how I verified it is value-free) and
#2126 (ordinary source under a secrets directory blocked without scoped
authorization). This request is the inverse of #2349: a scoped, declared
allow — not a hole.

### Proposed outcome

Project-scoped override: let a repo declare named form paths (e.g. in
`AGENTS.md`, which already declares such files readable) that the harness
trusts for those paths only. Value-bearing operations (`bao kv get`
values, `Secret .data`, converge env) stay fully gated. Expected behavior:
agent edits `secrets/contract.yaml` (form entry, no values); actual today:
blanket denial even with explicit in-chat user authorization.

### Alternatives considered

1. Human hand-inserts form YAML (works, 30s per entry, rare op — the
   current fallback; does not scale the documented agent workflow).
2. Repo-side merge task (`contract-add --file fragment`) so the agent never
   touches the path (respects the gate, but new code for a monthly op).
3. Hand-editing the global sensitive-path list (rejected: global blast
   radius for one repo's convenience, lost on harness updates, opens the
   list to sessions without the repo's doctrine).

### Additional context

- Environment: gentle-shell 4.4.0 agent; homelab repo with SOPS +
  ExternalSecrets contract lane, OpenBao KV v2 backend.
- Reproduction: in a repo whose skill orders contract edits, attempt
  read/edit of `secrets/contract.yaml` via agent tools → "Gentle AI safety
  policy blocked access to sensitive path", even with explicit user
  authorization in-chat.
- Concrete case: provisioning a `longhorn-s3-secret` ExternalSecret
  (missing BackupTarget credential → Longhorn `available:false`); blocked at
  skill step 1 (add contract entry).
- Acting identity for this report: agent credential (narrow, own login),
  never the human's.

items.title: Workout safety interrupts
items.body:
Interrupts that override the normal flow in any state (see "Safety interrupts" in `docs/workout-agent-loop.md`).

- [ ] Pain or "stop": `stop_motion`, say "Let's stop here," don't continue the exercise, flag the session for the therapist
- [ ] Patient leaves the camera view mid-set: pause mirroring, ask if they're OK, resume when they're back
- [ ] Servo too hot (API refuses motion): stop moving, explain the robot needs a rest, continue voice-only or end
- [ ] No response for a long time: ask once more, then end the session safely
- [ ] Decide what happens after pain: end the session, skip the exercise, or offer an easier version (open question in the doc)

items.title: Prototype: Prove the V2 agent execution and safety contract

labels.name: wayfinder:prototype
labels.description: Wayfinder ticket: HITL cheap artifact to react to

items.body:
## Question

Can the smallest public-API V2 execution adapter preserve ultraopen's validated agent returns and child containment without private APIs or a workflow-engine rewrite?

## Why this is a separate proof gate

[Pin the V2 port contract and preserve workflow guarantees](https://github.com/PhillipChaffee/ultraopen/issues/179#issuecomment-6397049576) identified three unresolved contracts in published V2.1.4: tool-using child-session structured output, safe permission-default precedence, and child-scoped shell recursion guards. These are core guarantees, not optional feature polish. API shape/source inference is not live proof.

Native prompt admission returns an inbox item, not the final assistant result. The checked V2 session API has no V1 `format`/`info.structured`. A custom tool's output schema and sessionless `generate.text` are not equivalent to a research-capable agent returning a validated object. Also, `shell.create.before` lacks a session ID, and nested CLI calls may reuse the service without rerunning plugin setup.

## Narrow prototype

Use an isolated V2 fixture plugin and a tiny plain+schema workflow, not a port of the whole product. Start with no-model fixture checks; explicitly account for any real-model calls and preserve artifacts/screenshots needed for Phillip's review.

Prove or reject a public terminal-result/capture-tool or other documented strategy that permits the child to research with normal tools before returning a validated value. Compare mechanisms with Phillip rather than silently choosing a provider-specific response format.

### Required observations

- A paid child can use a research tool first and return a validated object. Invalid output retries are bounded and stay in the same child context; cancellation/deadline does not restart it. Impossible schemas are rejected before creating/spending on a child. Plain/schema transcript readability and recording remain verifiable.
- Result correlation selects the admitted turn, not a stale last message. Tool output schema is not mistaken for model-return enforcement. Failed capture/validation retains existing failure semantics rather than parsing arbitrary prose and calling it guaranteed output.
- `workflow:ask` / `workflow_status:allow` defaults do not override explicit user denies/asks/allows. Permission errors propagate with V2's step-ending/feedback behavior rather than being swallowed by the old broad catch. This proves mechanics using explicit fixture policies; [the inheritance issue](https://github.com/PhillipChaffee/ultraopen/issues/149) still owns the user-facing policy decision.
- Engine-owned children cannot escape recursion/concurrency/budget boundaries by launching `opencode` through an absolute path, wrapper, or `sh -c`, in shared-service and standalone modes. Ordinary sessions are unaffected. Do not blanket-mark all shells or claim an inherited environment flag alone controls a reused service.
- Reload does not silently strand or duplicate the test execution. The [lifecycle research](https://github.com/PhillipChaffee/ultraopen/issues/180#issuecomment-6397043440) and lifetime decision remain authoritative; this small spike does not decide production recovery policy.

If a public path cannot preserve a guarantee, document the smallest missing upstream capability and block the corresponding implementation promise. Do not weaken schema validation, permission boundaries, or recursion protections to make the port appear complete.

## Close-out

This is a HITL feasibility/behavior prototype: link the artifact and observations, review them with Phillip, and record the chosen strategy or blocker. Throwaway proof is not a shipped adapter. Any code intended to ship requires local `bun run check` (95% coverage, Node parity), both real e2e suites at `0 failed`, PR opened with an honest Test Plan, CI green, merged. No live proof has run merely because this ticket exists.

Define explicit global/node/project/agent configuration contexts and process-lifetime runtime overrides. Preserve ADR-0004 repo policy domains, common-directory authority and additive safety floors; display names never select a scope. No fleet replication or arbitrary-path writes.

After acceptance, split into separate <=400-production-line PRs for: context IDs and scope admission; scoped file resolution through resolve_write_target; deterministic scope/layer resolution; runtime override ownership and lifecycle; actual client/GUI scope addressing. Tests must use real loader/API paths where data crosses subsystems.

items.title: [Platform] Add absolute compaction token ceilings with world, agent, and conversation overrides

labels.name: priority:medium
labels.description: Medium priority - fix in next cycle

labels.name: source:user-feedback
labels.description: User feedback - high signal, needs attention

items.body:
## Outcome

Let users choose when BotNexus compacts working context independently of a model's advertised context-window capacity. Provide a world-wide default, optional agent overrides, and optional conversation overrides.

A larger supported context window must not automatically force users to retain a larger working context. Capacity and preferred working-context size are different concerns.

## Approved product direction

Jon requested this hierarchy and an issue detailing the work on 2026-10-13:

1. World-wide compaction token ceiling.
2. Agent override, otherwise inherit the world value.
3. Conversation override, otherwise inherit the agent/world value.

No production ceiling value has been chosen. Numeric examples below are illustrative, not an instruction to deploy those values. This issue authorizes planning; implementation and deployment are separate steps.

## Current source-backed behavior

- `src/gateway/BotNexus.Gateway.Contracts/Sessions/CompactionOptions.cs` exposes `TokenThresholdRatio` (default 0.6) and `ContextWindowTokens`, but no independent absolute token ceiling.
- `LlmSessionCompactor.EvaluateTokenTriggers` in `src/gateway/BotNexus.Gateway/Sessions/LlmSessionCompactor.cs` calculates `context window × ratio`; either the local visible-history estimate or a known provider prompt-token count can trigger compaction.
- `SessionContextWindowResolver.cs` and `ScopedCompactionWindow` in `ISessionContextWindowResolver.cs` resolve the effective context window from conversation, agent, and model. A known scoped/model window replaces the global compaction fallback window.
- `GatewayHost.PrepareTurnAsync` checks pre-turn compaction. `InProcessIsolationStrategy` also checks compaction between loop iterations and replaces the live agent context after an applied compaction. Both paths need the same resolved ceiling policy.
- Compacted transcript entries remain stored as historical records; total stored message count is not the live context size.

This is a new policy control, not a claim that existing compaction failed. Related work #4307 reduces tool-output context growth; this issue independently controls the preferred compaction trigger.

## Configuration and inheritance contract

Introduce a nullable positive integer setting, proposed name `compactionTokenCeiling`, expressed in tokens. The final serialized naming should follow existing world/agent/conversation configuration conventions.

| Scope | Behavior |
|---|---|
| World | Default ceiling for agents/conversations in that world. Do not accidentally apply one world's value to another. |
| Agent | Explicit value replaces the inherited world ceiling. Unset inherits. |
| Conversation | Explicit value replaces the inherited agent/world ceiling. Unset inherits. |

Resolve the ceiling as `conversation ?? agent ?? world`. The setting is a default with overrides, not an administrator-enforced maximum: a more specific scope may choose a larger ceiling, subject to the model safety threshold.

Null/unset means inherit. If every scope is unset, retain existing ratio-based behavior. Reject zero, negative, non-integral, and out-of-range values through all write surfaces; do not overload zero as disable/inherit. Provide an explicit reset-to-inherited action.

Keep this setting separate from `contextWindow`: users should not have to misrepresent model capacity to choose an earlier compaction point.

## Trigger semantics

```text
ratioThreshold = floor(effectiveContextWindowTokens × tokenThresholdRatio)
resolvedCeiling = conversation ceiling ?? agent ceiling ?? world ceiling
effectiveThreshold = resolvedCeiling is set
    ? min(ratioThreshold, resolvedCeiling)
    : ratioThreshold
```

Use the same effective threshold for the local-estimate trigger, known provider prompt-token trigger, and the compactor's above-threshold fallback/cut planning. A ceiling cannot bypass the existing smaller-model safety threshold.

Example: a model with a 922,000-token window and ratio 0.6 has a ratio threshold of 553,200 tokens. With a world ceiling of 100,000, it should compact at the 100,000-token policy threshold rather than waiting for 553,200. A conversation override of 150,000 changes that conversation's ceiling only. A smaller model whose ratio threshold is 76,800 still compacts at 76,800.

Preserve the existing independent oversized-entry trigger and its suppression safeguards.

This is a proactive compaction trigger, not a promise that no request can ever exceed the chosen token count: measurements can be estimated or lag by one provider call, and tool outputs can arrive in bursts. Document these limits explicitly. Do not silently truncate messages or alter model output limits to enforce the setting.

## UI, persistence, and diagnostics

- Expose the world setting in the appropriate world configuration surface, the agent override in agent settings, and the conversation override under advanced conversation settings.
- Display explicit versus inherited value, source scope, effective safety threshold, and resulting compaction threshold.
- Example: `Compaction trigger: 100,000 tokens — ceiling inherited from World; model safety threshold: 553,200`.
- Persist agent/conversation overrides and round-trip them through APIs, configuration/export/import, and restart according to existing scope conventions.
- Re-evaluate at the next safe compaction check after a settings change, including for an already-running long dispatch. Do not abort a currently executing tool just to apply a setting.
- Report estimate/provider measurement availability distinctly. Unknown provider usage must remain unknown, not zero.
- Logs/context diagnostics must identify resolved ceiling, source scope, ratio threshold, effective threshold, measurement, and trigger reason without prompt contents or secrets.

## Acceptance criteria

1. World, agent, and conversation support a nullable positive integer token ceiling with consistent validation, persistence, and API/UI round-trip behavior.
2. Tests prove precedence, reset/inheritance, world isolation, and independent settings for sibling agents/conversations.
3. With no ceiling anywhere, existing behavior is unchanged. Existing configurations migrate without selecting an arbitrary new ceiling.
4. A large-model fixture with a 100,000 ceiling triggers above that threshold even though its ratio threshold is 553,200. Boundary tests cover below/equal/above using the existing comparison convention consistently.
5. A more specific larger ceiling is honored, but never raises the threshold above the model-window ratio safety threshold.
6. Both known provider counts and local estimates use the same effective threshold. Tests cover unavailable/stale provider measurements without inventing usage.
7. Pre-turn and mid-loop paths resolve the same policy; setting changes become effective at the next safe check without requiring a fresh conversation or stopping an active tool.
8. Split/fallback planning uses the same threshold as the trigger, including low-user-turn/high-tool-volume cases. No trigger/skip disagreement or repeated no-op loop is introduced.
9. Compaction resynchronizes live context and retains historical transcript data. A huge stored transcript does not independently trigger compaction merely because historical entries remain in the database.
10. Oversized-entry behavior, conflict handling, circuit breaker, cancellation, and fail-closed proactive compaction safeguards remain intact.
11. UI shows the effective trigger and inheritance source, permits reset to inherited, and has component tests for editing, validation, inheritance, and error states.
12. Tests cover invalid values, model changes, smaller-model safety, override removal, and a ceiling below irreducible prompt overhead. Unsatisfiable context reduction is reported through existing explicit failure/skip safeguards rather than an unbounded compaction loop; the UI/documentation must not promise a hard request-size cap.
13. Documentation explains working-context ceiling versus model capacity, scope precedence, compatibility/defaults, token-measurement limitations, and trigger versus hard-cap semantics.

## Delivery shape

Keep the work in small reviewable slices if needed:

1. Configuration/persistence and one shared scoped policy resolver.
2. Trigger/cut-plan integration for pre-turn and mid-loop paths with deterministic regression tests.
3. World/agent/conversation UI and diagnostics/documentation.

Do not consider the feature complete after only adding a global field: the approved scope includes inheritance, both execution paths, observability, and the user-facing controls.

## Out of scope

- Selecting or deploying Jon's preferred numeric ceiling.
- Changing model registry context-window capacities.
- Replacing the compaction summarizer or retention algorithm.
- Destructive transcript trimming or a strict provider-request admission cap.
- Implementing the queryable tool-result store from #4307.
- Updating, rebuilding, or restarting a running gateway as part of issue creation.

items.title: Reliability backlog: ownership safety, agent compatibility, and workflow improvements
items.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

# Prioritized Reliability Backlog

Consolidated follow-ups from the October review, ordered by expected impact.
This is a selection backlog, not approval to implement everything automatically.
It excludes the selected Zsh compilation, CI runtime, and advisory-expiry work.

The goal remains a repeatable personal Ubuntu/WSL environment that preserves
existing setups, keeps authentication manual, and validates changes in Docker.

## 1. Completed: Make MCP JSON Updates Safe Around Symlinks and Permissions

**Resolved:** #38 in `678fa2d`; [final CI passed at `783a49e`](https://github.com/Idanbot/.dotfiles/actions/runs/40503227642). The following describes the original bug.

**Why:** The current JSON updater reads a config through a symlink, obtains the
link's mode with `stat`, and applies that mode to a new regular file. A typical
symlink reports `0777`, which can turn private configuration into a broadly
accessible replacement. Existing over-permissive regular files are also retained.

**Example:** A user keeps OMP's MCP config in a separate private location and
symlinks it into the agent directory. `agent-mcp enable serena --agent omp`
must not silently replace the link or publish a mode-0777 config.

**Acceptance:**
- [x] Choose and document a conservative symlink policy: refuse by default, or require explicit target handling.
- [x] Use private staging and safe regular-file permissions; preserve unrelated JSON settings and the original on errors.
- [x] Docker regressions cover normal/private files, permissive files, symlinks, dangling links, and redirected parents.

## 2. High: Reconcile OMP/Pix Compatibility and Keep It Tested

**Evidence:** [Release smoke in run 39745980023](https://github.com/Idanbot/.dotfiles/actions/runs/39745980023/job/119716571504)
fails while installing `@xynogen/pix-optimizer@1.3.2`. The declared OMP pin is
`18.10.1`. Extension validation reports that `hyperlink` is not exported by
`omp-legacy-pi-bundled:@oh-my-pi/pi-tui`. The fast contract checks passed, but
the live gate correctly blocked subsequent installation acceptance.

**Why:** An agent and its extension are a compatibility pair, not two independent
version numbers. A failed extension install can block the AI/full profile.

**Example:** An upgrade report proposes a Pix release whose imports are absent
from the OMP API exposed by the committed agent version.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] Reproduce the committed pair in a disposable container and identify whether the mismatch is direct or transitive dependency drift.
- [ ] Select a tested compatible pair or change the integration deliberately; do not ignore extension validation or weaken the live gate.
- [ ] Exercise real extension installation and loading in release/full acceptance, and prevent grouped upgrades from presenting incompatible pairs as validated.

## 3. High: Apply Ownership Checks Before Package-Manager Uninstalls

**Why:** Direct-file removal verifies ownership, but npm, uv/Python, and OMP
uninstall branches currently delegate to the manager without the same digest
and installation-identity rechecks. An old ledger entry is not proof that the
current environment is still owned by dotfiles.

**Example:** Dotfiles records a managed CLI, the user later replaces its
environment manually, then `dot uninstall <tool>` removes that replacement.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] Verify the recorded prefix/environment, current manager ownership, and relevant digests before invoking removal.
- [ ] Refuse modified, unverifiable, redirected, or externally replaced installations without changing their ledger entries.
- [ ] Cover unchanged managed removal, changed environments, stale ledgers, shared caches, and dry-run parity with synthetic manager fixtures.

## 4. Completed: Make Download-Cache Pruning Respect Active Locks

**Resolved:** #41 in `dd60aa5`; [CI passed](https://github.com/Idanbot/.dotfiles/actions/runs/40386856337). The following describes the original bug.

**Why:** Pruning currently removes old object files and deletes old lock files
without coordinating with readers/downloaders. Deleting a locked file's pathname
can let another process create a different lock inode for the same cache key.

**Example:** A download holds an old SHA256 lock; pruning deletes its pathname;
a second download opens a new lock and both proceed concurrently.

**Acceptance:**
- [x] Preserve lock identity and coordinate pruning with per-object and verification-material locks; skip busy entries.
- [x] Keep payload/verification metadata consistent and avoid deleting staging files belonging to active operations.
- [x] Add a deterministic Docker test that holds an artificially old lock while prune and a second reader run.

## 5. Medium: Add Explicit Offline Isolation for Catalog Version Probes

**Why:** Receipts already avoid executing binaries, but a separate catalog
refresh executes installed version commands with inherited environment and
home access. Some commands check for upstream updates even for `--version`.

**Example:** A catalog refresh invokes a version command that contacts an update
service or initializes configuration. An offline request should not silently
allow those side effects.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] Design an explicit offline probe mode with bounded runtime, sanitized environment, and enforceable network/filesystem limits.
- [ ] Report unavailable isolation honestly instead of claiming a sandbox that is not supported on that machine.
- [ ] Keep receipts non-executing and add fixture binaries that attempt a request or a write; never use actual user configuration as test input.

## 6. Medium: Provide a Manual Authentication-Readiness Checklist

**Why:** A working binary is different from a ready-to-use authenticated tool.
GitHub readiness has a check, but there is no unified provider/agent checklist.
Fresh installation must still succeed without any credentials.

**Example:** An optional report distinguishes AWS SSO login needed, Azure login
needed, and a configured-but-not-verified Kubernetes context, then suggests
native commands such as `aws sso login --profile <profile>`.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] Keep it opt-in, advisory, and read-only; never automate login/logout, key creation, credential import, or bootstrap secrets.
- [ ] Distinguish installed, locally configured, and remotely verified states; require explicit consent for network verification.
- [ ] Emit fixed status codes and generic native next steps by default, not tokens, account IDs, project names, or context contents; test with mocks only.

## 7. Medium: Add a Concise Repository-Specific Agent Playbook

**Why:** Canonical global agent instructions are deployed, but the repository
has no root `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` defining this project's exact engineering and
privacy rules. Global shell/tool preferences do not explain its CI gates or
ownership model.

**Example:** A new contributor should learn immediately to use Docker suites,
edit templates rather than deployed files, preserve local state, and keep
authentication manual.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] Choose one root playbook and link the existing architecture/ADRs and authoritative Docker entrypoints.
- [ ] State GitHub issue conventions, source-versus-destination ownership, generated-file rules, and explicit approval requirements for publishing private data.
- [ ] Keep it short and avoid copying the README or global instructions into another divergent document.

## 8. Medium: Add Workspace Presets With a Review-Only Drift Preview

**Why:** The common agent registry and backend routing work, but different tasks
need different selections/layouts. Repeatedly editing one global workspace
definition makes experiments harder to reproduce safely.

**Example:** A `review` preset could open a terminal, Codex, and Claude, while
an `implementation` preset uses a different agent subset. A proposed command
such as `dot workspace --preset review --plan` should show changes without
altering live panes or processes. This interface is illustrative, not implemented.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] Define declarative presets that reuse the existing registry and backend-aware nesting rules.
- [ ] Preview additions/changes before applying; preserve active user sessions and local overrides by default.
- [ ] Cover both backends, repeated application, missing agents, paths with spaces, and non-mutating previews in disposable fixtures.

## Guardrails

Use synthetic data and Docker/disposable systems for every regression test.
Do not attach real machine inventories, raw shell/SSH/cloud configs, credentials,

items.title: feat(config): override a config value from the command line
items.body:
Every devkit command that loads a config accepts a repeatable `-o/--option KEY=VALUE`, such as `-o tracker.kind="github"`. The value parses as TOML and merges as the highest layer, over the discovered layers or over `--config`. A one-off run or a test can then change one key without a second config file. `--config` replaces the whole layer stack, so a run that names one file loses keys the other files set, such as `[tracker] kind`.

`workspace sync-includes` gives up its `-o` short flag, so `-o` means `--option` on every command. Its `--overwrite` long flag stays.

An agent caller is refused `--option`. Several keys are safety controls (`[harness]` enforcement, the PR gates, fidelity), and the flag would let an agent weaken them in one command.

## Done when

- [ ] `devkit config show -o tracker.kind="none"` in a checkout whose `devkit.toml` sets `kind = "github"` prints `kind = "none"` (proof: test <name>)
- [ ] `--option` merges over the file `--config` names, and a repeated `--option` for the same key keeps the last (proof: test <name>)
- [ ] `devkit config show --origin` names the command line as the source of an overridden key (proof: test <name>)
- [ ] A value that is not valid TOML, or a key the schema does not know, fails the command and names the key (proof: test <name>)
- [ ] An agent caller that passes `--option` is refused with a message that names the flag (proof: test <name>)
- [ ] `workspace sync-includes -o` reads `-o` as `--option`, and `workspace sync-includes --overwrite` still overwrites (proof: test <name>)

## Stop and ask if

- A natural set of policy keys appears that would let agents override the other keys safely. Ask before allowing agents any `--option`.

## Out of scope

- An environment variable that carries overrides into hooks and child processes.
- Refusing `--config` and `$DEVKIT_CONFIG` for agent callers, though they can replace the same policy keys.

## Context

Prior art: alacritree's `-o/--option`, merged over both its config files.

items.title: [Epic][Latency] Cut safety-induced latency without cutting safety coverage — instrument, split, speculate

labels.name: python
labels.description: Pull requests that update python code

labels.name: CHI paper
labels.description: Tracked for the CHI asymmetric-help paper

items.body:
## Summary

Reduce **safety-induced latency without reducing safety coverage** in the Stella V2 turn pipeline, by *reordering* the work rather than *skipping* it. Three sequenced steps: **instrument → split the pool into blocking / non-blocking → speculate**.

This is an epic. Each step is a sub-issue and independently shippable; the ordering matters because step 1 is the evidence base for steps 2 and 3 (and is the ablation the CUI paper owes).

## The claim we want to be able to make

> STELLA reduces safety-induced latency **without reducing safety coverage.**

Every expert still runs, every verdict is still logged, arbitration is unchanged. Latency drops because the critical path shrinks — not because checks were dropped.

## The alternative we are explicitly rejecting

A **semantic cascade** — e.g. an embedding/familiarity classifier that decides "this input looks like inputs we've safely handled before, skip the expert pool this turn." This is worth writing down because it is the obvious first idea and it is the wrong one:

- It **creates a coverage hole.** A skipped expert produces no verdict, so there is nothing to audit and no way to bound the miss rate after the fact.
- The saving is the same as speculative execution, which has no hole.
- It is a weak scientific claim. "We skip the experts when an embedding says the input looks familiar" invites exactly the reviewer question we cannot answer: *what did you miss?*

Speculative execution buys the same wall-clock at the cost of some discarded generations — a cost we can *measure* directly from logs and tune, rather than a coverage risk we can only hope is small.

## Investigation findings (current pipeline, as of this issue)

Turn flow lives in `agents/stella-v2-agent/src/stella_v2_agent/agent.py::process` (~`:178-510`) and is, in wall-clock order:

| Stage | Code | Concurrency today |
|---|---|---|
| Context fetch (history + `sm_context` over gRPC) | `agent.py:206-212` | serial, uninstrumented |
| Stage 1 — Bridge (LLM, streamed) | `agent.py:253-299` | **serial** ahead of experts |
| Stage 2 — Expert Pool | `agent.py:311-317`, `pipeline/expert_pool.py:110-131` | experts parallel with each other, blocking the turn |
| Stage 3 — Arbitration (pure Python) | `agent.py:348-353`, `pipeline/arbitration.py:99-253` | ~1ms, serial |
| Stage 4 — Response Generator (LLM, streamed) | `agent.py:419-484` | serial |

Three concrete findings that shape the sub-issues:

1. **The bridge does not actually overlap the expert pool.** The module docstring (`agent.py:4-5`) claims "The Bridge Generator runs concurrently with this stage to mask latency" — but `async for bridge_accum in ...generate_stream(...)` at `agent.py:270` is fully drained before `expert_pool.run()` is awaited at `agent.py:312`. Bridge *playback* overlaps the experts (TTS happens downstream in the SDK audio loop); bridge *generation* does not. With `BRIDGE_FAST_PATH` defaulting to `False` (`bridge_generator.py:399`) that is a whole `gpt-4o-mini` call sitting in front of the pool. → #455.

2. **The priority hierarchy is already a usable scheduling primitive — and so are `verdict_directives`.** Whether an expert can *veto* a response is statically declarable from its config: only `override` / `short_circuit` actions replace the reply (`experts/base.py:15`, `VERDICT_ACTIONS`). Today: `noise_detection` (prio 100, `unclear → short_circuit`), `medical` (95, `critical → override`, `high → prepend`), `legal` (90, same shape) can veto; `task_extraction` (70), `probing` (60), `timekeeper` (50) are `inform`-only — they shape content, they never block it. → #456.

3. **We cannot currently justify any of this from data.** Per-expert `latency_ms` and arbitration `latency_ms` exist in memory (`models/expert_verdict.py:36`, `models/arbitration_result.py`) and are persisted — but as `messageType='debug'` rows, invisible to the analytics stage aggregator (`src/agents/agents.service.ts::extractStageTiming:1094`). There is no `expert_pool` or `arbitration` timeline event at all. → #454, which must land first.

## Sub-issues

- **#454 — Instrument** — per-stage timing on every turn: context fetch, bridge generation, bridge playback duration, each expert individually, arbitration, response first-token, TTS first-chunk. This is also the ablation the CUI paper owes; no argument below is defensible without it.
- **#455 — Overlap the bridge with the pool** — small, independent, and the cheapest win on the list. Discovered during this investigation.
- **#456 — Two-tier expert scheduling** — only veto-capable experts gate response generation. Non-vetoing experts still run, still log, still arbitrate; they just stop sitting on the critical path. Critical path collapses toward the fastest, smallest expert.
- **#457 — Speculative generation** — start the substantive response concurrently with the blocking tier. No override fires → already streamed. Override fires before TTS onset → discard and regenerate.

## Acceptance criteria (epic level)

- A per-turn latency breakdown exists in the analytics path and is chartable, before/after each change.
- Every enabled expert still runs on every turn and still emits a verdict — measurable from the logs, not asserted.
- Measured reduction in time-to-first-substantive-token, reported with the ablation from A.
- No expert with an `override` / `short_circuit` verdict directive can be bypassed by any of these changes; a test asserts it.

## Out of scope

- Any form of check-skipping: familiarity/embedding cascades, sampling experts, "safe input" fast lanes.
- Changing what the experts *decide* (prompt/model quality work) — this epic is purely about *when* they run.

items.title: [WAYFINDER MAP 2] Agent Guardrails - pre-action safety checks
items.body:
## Destination

An **agent guardrail library** for TypeScript: a pre-action check that decides, before a tool call executes, whether the action should proceed, be refused, or be escalated to a human.

It is imported into agents you write yourself. It is not a service, not a harness plugin, not a dashboard. It never executes tools, never merges, never deploys.

Ship shape: one TypeScript package under `projects/agent-guardrails/` with `guard(tools)` as the primary surface, `check()` as the escape hatch, a deterministic rules layer in front of a three-proposition System One judge, and a fail-closed escalation path that reaches you through an outbound webhook.

## Invariants

Load-bearing. A ticket that breaks one is wrong even if its tests pass.

1. **Rules precede the model.** `allow` skips the judge entirely, `block` is final, `abstain` hands off. The model can never overrule a rule, and no audit row ever records a judgment that was subsequently ignored.
2. **The model escalates, never blocks.** `block` is reserved for the deterministic layer. A calibrated low probability must not hard-stop work.
3. **Fail closed everywhere.** Timeout, malformed answer, missing key, provider outage, unknown verb: all escalate. There is no fail-open configuration flag, and none may be added.
4. **Denial is a tool result, not an exception.** The guarded tool never executes, and the agent receives a structured result so its loop survives and can revise.
5. **Evidence is observed, not asserted.** Declared evidence is supplementary. A sufficiency verdict resting only on declared evidence can never return `proceed`.
6. **Redaction is structural.** The state type cannot carry a payload. There is no `content`, `body`, or `output` field to forget. Regex scrubbing is a backup, never the mechanism.
7. **No persistence.** No SQLite, no file writes by default, no queue. Events go to a caller-supplied sink. The audit record carries no task text and no evidence refs.
8. **Budgets are hard.** 3000 ms total per check, 1200 ms per provider attempt, at most 2 attempts. A second attempt starts only after a fast failure, never after budget exhaustion.
9. **Only the calibrated judge may grant permission.** A transport fallback to the same model may proceed. A fallback to a different model may escalate but never proceed.
10. **Permission is granted locally.** Approval tokens are single-use and scoped to `(sessionId, actionHash)` with a TTL. Nothing on the network can mint one.
11. **Code owns composition.** The judge supplies three probabilities. Code does every threshold comparison, margin, reason-code selection and verdict.
12. **Default rules block almost nothing.** Exactly four blocking defaults, each unambiguously destructive. Everything else abstains.
13. **No verdict cache and no optimistic mode.** A verdict is never reused across calls, and no action runs before its check completes.

## Decisions so far

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| 1 | TypeScript library at `projects/agent-guardrails/`, own `package.json`, Bun, ESM, zero native deps, Node + Bun targets. No root workspace wiring, so `uv.lock` and the Python pipeline stay untouched |
| 2 | Two layers. Deterministic rules resolve what they can with zero network; the judge receives only the residual |
| 3 | Evidence is a hybrid: `observed` items are auto-captured from the guarded call stream and are primary; `declared` items are supplementary and can never alone justify `proceed` |
| 4 | Three propositions, all high-means-safe: `context_sufficient` (>= 0.60), `intent_match` (>= 0.75), `unambiguous` (>= 0.75). Composition is conjunctive, never a weighted sum |
| 5 | Judge output can only escalate. A malformed or missing answer is `judge_unusable` and escalates |
| 6 | Rules return `allow` / `block` / `abstain`. `allow` means do not consult the judge, not override the judge |
| 7 | 3000 ms total, 1200 ms per provider, max 2 attempts, timeout escalates. No verdict cache, no optimistic execution anywhere |
| 8 | Judge chain: Clef-Flash primary, then Jev 1.13 via OpenRouter, then Jev via Vercel AI Gateway, then Laya Free. Only a same-model transport fallback may return `proceed` |
| 9 | Escalation is fail-closed: structured denial as a tool result, an `ApprovalRequest` plain object, single-use scoped token with TTL, bounded wait that denies on timeout |
| 10 | Surface is `guard(tools)` primary plus `check()` escape hatch. Plain `{name, description, execute}` tool objects, framework-agnostic. Adapters for AI SDK / OpenAI / LangChain are out of scope |
| 11 | Eval is 60 cases: 20 safe, 20 unsafe, 15 hard negatives, 5 ambiguous. Gate is two-sided: zero false-allows on unsafe + hard negatives, benign escalate rate <= 10%. Thresholds are calibrated from the run, not inherited |
| 12 | Redaction by construction. Refs never payloads, repo-relative paths, task truncated at 2000 chars, audit carries no state, refuse to run in a browser |
| 13 | Delivery is an outbound webhook with a Discord formatter. Approval happens locally only. v1 never accepts permission from the network |
| 14 | Exactly four blocking defaults: delete outside worktree, secret-file read, force-push to a protected branch, `reset --hard` or `clean -fd` with uncommitted tracked changes. Package install, spend, deploy and external sends abstain |
| 15 | Cost model: rules path is free and sub-5 ms. Judge path is one call carrying all three questions |
| 16 | Failure vocabulary is a closed `ReasonCode` enum. No free-text reasons reach the consumer |
| 17 | Adversarial input is mitigated structurally: state carries refs, not content, so injected instructions have almost no surface. Unreadable state is `judge_unusable`, never a pass |
| 18 | Deferred deliberately: dashboard, ClickUp/Obsidian/cron delivery, SQLite, framework adapters, ensemble fanout, threshold auto-tuning, policy DSL, HTTP service, OpenCode/T3 plugin, per-session cost accounting, multimodal state |

## Provisional numbers (not decisions)

The three thresholds (0.60 / 0.75 / 0.75), the 60-case split, the 10% benign-escalate ceiling, the 2000-character task bound, the 5-minute token TTL and the 10-minute approval wait are **guesses wearing numbers**. Ticket 12 replaces the thresholds with values measured on the eval set. Do not treat the defaults as considered.

## Child Tickets & Frontier DAG

All thirteen tickets are `[TASK:AFK]`. Native sub-issue links and `blocked by` edges are set on the tracker.

| Wave | Ticket | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | [#19 Scaffold the TypeScript package and the structural guards](https://github.com/parth5012/system-one-projects/issues/19) | none |
| 1 | [#20 Types, verdict vocabulary, state assembly, and redaction by construction](https://github.com/parth5012/system-one-projects/issues/20) | #19 |
| 2 | [#21 Audit sinks: memory ring buffer and opt-in JSONL](https://github.com/parth5012/system-one-projects/issues/21) | #20 |
| 2 | [#22 Deterministic rules engine with exactly four blocking defaults](https://github.com/parth5012/system-one-projects/issues/22) | #20 |
| 2 | [#23 Judge client: three propositions, four-tier chain, hard budget](https://github.com/parth5012/system-one-projects/issues/23) | #20 |
| 3 | [#24 Composition: conjunctive thresholds and reason codes](https://github.com/parth5012/system-one-projects/issues/24) | #23 |
| 4 | [#25 guard(tools) wrapper, evidence capture, and the check() escape hatch](https://github.com/parth5012/system-one-projects/issues/25) | #22, #23, #24 |
| 5 | [#26 Approval store, single-use scoped tokens, bounded wait](https://github.com/parth5012/system-one-projects/issues/26) | #25 |
| 5 | [#28 Eval harness: case schema, runner, and the two-sided gate](https://github.com/parth5012/system-one-projects/issues/28) | #24, #25 |
| 6 | [#27 Outbound webhook and Discord delivery, no inbound surface](https://github.com/parth5012/system-one-projects/issues/27) | #26 |
| 6 | [#29 Author the 60 eval cases including 15 hard negatives](https://github.com/parth5012/system-one-projects/issues/29) | #28 |
| 7 | [#30 Threshold calibration, gate proof, and the drift probe](https://github.com/parth5012/system-one-projects/issues/30) | #29 |
| 7 | [#31 Design record, README, and the runnable minimal-agent example](https://github.com/parth5012/system-one-projects/issues/31) | #25, #27 |

Wave 2 is the only genuine parallelism: three tickets, disjoint files, no shared state. Everything else is serial because later tickets compile against earlier types.

## Handover Notes

- Every ticket is self-contained: goal, exact files, behavioural requirements, acceptance criteria, invariants. An agent can pick one up cold with no session history.
- All tickets are `[TASK:AFK]`. This map has no HITL tickets, so Phase 1 is empty and the runner goes straight to Phase 2.
- T1 through T12 change code. That is 12 code-changing AFK tickets, so the runner must use **stacked-PR mode**, one branch and one PR per ticket, base = parent branch, in topo order.
- Parallelism: T3, T4 and T5 all depend only on T2 and can run in parallel. T6 depends on T5. Nothing else parallelises safely.
- This is TypeScript, not Python. The repo TDD rule still binds: red, green, refactor, no implementation before a failing test. But the commands are `bun test` and `bunx tsc --noEmit` from `projects/agent-guardrails/`. There is no `pyproject.toml` entry to add and none may be added.
- Do not modify `projects/email-triage`. It is the reference for pattern, not a shared library. Port the provider-call shapes into TypeScript rather than depending on Python.
- The core must import no `node:fs` and no `node:child_process`. Filesystem and git state arrive through the injected `Hooks` interface in T4. A test enforces this, because Workers compatibility depends on it.
- Unit tests must make zero network calls. Inject a fake transport everywhere, and assert the fake was never called on the paths that should not reach the judge.
- A ticket that finds the design wrong should comment on this map rather than silently deviate. Deviations are decisions and belong in the record.
- **Tracker pitfall, verified:** `gh issue list --search "parent:18"` returns tickets from map 1 as well, because that qualifier does not resolve sub-issue edges. Read children with `gh issue view 18 --json subIssues` instead, and read edges with `gh issue view <N> --json blockedBy,parent`. The runner's Step 1 fallback must not be used here.
- The map number is **18**. It is the second map in this repo; map 1 (#1) covers PR risk gating and shares no code, no labels beyond `wayfinder:*`, and no `subsystem:` label.

items.title: Embedded-instruction override resistance: split grounding-conflict vs instruction-injection, override-resistance as hard gate
items.body:
**Source:** eval_4 ch.4 — multimodal safety evaluation as a hard training gate; hidden text / embedded-instruction handling. Book identity unverified (chapter text only). [adaptation]

**Mechanism (clean-room, neutral domain):** Visual or file-embedded content introduces an instruction vector that prompt-only safety evaluation cannot anticipate: text rendered inside an image/document can act as an instruction. The chapter splits two cases that must be measured separately:

1. **Embedded text contradicting the visible evidence** → a *grounding conflict* (the text says one thing, the image shows another). Measured against grounding metrics.
2. **Embedded text acting as an instruction** → a *prompt-injection* (the model must follow its system prompt, not the embedded instruction). Measured as a safety gate.

Collapsing the two hides the failure mode: a suite that only checks "did the model describe the image correctly" will miss a model that was silently redirected by embedded instructions while describing them accurately.

The hard-gate mechanism:

- **Override-resistance rate:** percentage of embedded-instruction cases where the agent follows its configured instructions and ignores the injected ones, tested at varying prominence levels (obvious overlay → subtle footer text → OCR-layer-only).
- **Injection success rate:** must be at or near zero on the defined probe set; any success is a hard block, not compensable by quality scores (safety is not weighted against grounding fidelity).
- **Refusal behavior on adversarial inputs:** refusal rate on inputs designed to elicit unsafe outputs through the visual/file channel, with an explicit threshold floor per deployment exposure.

**Acceptance criteria (theory-level — simplistic fallbacks forbidden):**

- Chaos scenario set contains embedded-instruction probes at ≥3 prominence levels; each probe names which of the two cases it tests (grounding-conflict vs instruction-injection).
- Override-resistance and injection-success are reported as separate metrics; a blended "safety score" is rejected.
- Any injection success on the defined set blocks the candidate — hard gate, no override path through quality or efficiency scores.
- Probe set is versioned; results record the probe-set version so a later-expanded set doesn't silently move the goalposts.

**Duplicates check:** complements #63 (adversarial literature patterns as chaos scenarios — this adds the specific embedded-instruction vector with its two-case split and metrics), #72 (trust-context inbound scanner — detection layers, not the override-resistance behavioral gate), #77 (calibration-aware escalation — guardrail decisions, not injection resistance). No overlap.

items.title: [Safety Parent] Execution Safety KernelとGuarded/Optional Policyを分離する

labels.name: P1
labels.description: 普通の優先タスク・主要経路・必須前提

items.body:
## 種別
実装 / Safety / Execution Boundary / Expert Override

## 概要
Safety機能を「全部削除不能なPipeline Stage」として扱わず、以下の3階層へ分離する。

1. **LOCKED — Execution Safety Kernel**
2. **GUARDED — Expertが警告付きで無効化可能なSafety Policy**
3. **OPTIONAL — 品質/信頼性向上用の通常Stage**

本当に外せない安全機能はFlow Graph内のStageではなく、すべての実入力が最後に通るExecution BoundaryとしてFlowの外側へ置く。

## Product Principle
**Expert may recompose the brain, but cannot remove the minimal input containment boundary.**

```text
User Flow / MOD / Script / Models
             |
             v
        Action Proposal
             |
             v
   +----------------------+
   | Execution Safety     |  <- LOCKED / non-bypassable
   | Kernel               |
   +----------------------+
             |
             v
          Executor
             |
             v
            OS
```

Flow側にSafety Stageを置くだけではbranch/replace設定で迂回可能になるため、KernelはExecutor入口そのものへ統合する。

## LOCKED — Execution Safety Kernel
削除・disable・bypass不可。

最低限以下を含む。

### Emergency Stop / release
- inference/model/pluginから独立したEmergency Stop
- held key/mouseのbounded TTL
- release-all
- Stop/cancel優先

### Runtime lease / liveness
- stale heartbeat/leaseで入力停止
- crash/deadlock時に入力継続しない
- restart後にACTIVEを自動復元しない

### Authorized target boundary
- target/session identity validation
- authorized HWND/PID/target set外へ入力しない
- client-area / declared target region境界
- single-window固定ではなく、必要ならauthorized target scopeを設定可能にする

### Command freshness / identity
- action/session/epoch/generation整合
- duplicate/stale command拒否
- bounded command age

### Action structural validity
- Action schema/type/range validation
- selected actionが現在許可されたAction contract内であること
- malformed/NaN/out-of-range等を拒否

### Fail closed
- Kernel自身が例外/不明状態なら実行しない
- Kernelを通らないdirect OS input pathを公式Plugin capabilityとして提供しない

## GUARDED — Expert override可能
通常は有効。Expert/Developerなら明示警告・Profile記録付きでdisable/relax可能。

候補:

### Semantic / behavioral risk
- #22 destructive/irreversible Action評価
- goal alignment
- suspicious Action追加verification

### Decision reliability
- #43のreason/action contradiction等
- semantic verifier
- additional agreement requirement

ただし#43のうちAction ID/schema/stale groundingのようにKernelと重複するstructural validationはLOCKED側へ残す。

### Repetition / no-progress
- repeat/cycle detector
- action count/session duration soft limit
- no-progress escalation

### Rate / burst policy
- 通常のclick/key rate ceiling
- debounce / burst制限

ただしhold TTL / emergency releaseのhard ceilingはLOCKED。

### Target confidence / stability
- #402 multi-frame target stability
- extra re-observe requirement
- confidence threshold

ただしauthorized target / stale command境界はLOCKED。

### Dangerous key policy
- deny-list / caution-list

ゲーム固有キーとの衝突があり得るため、Expert profileでは個別override可能にする。
OS/runtimeとして絶対送るべきでない入力がある場合のみKernel側へ分類する。

## OPTIONAL
無効化しても入力containmentを壊さない品質向上Stage。

例:
- Self-Check
- Unknownness policy
- extra semantic verifier
- additional observation
- Brain Message
- ensemble
- optional risk heuristics
- exploration controls
- optional OCR/VLM passes

## Expert Override UX
GUARDED機能をdisable/relaxする場合:

- 何を外すか
- 想定risk
- 対象Player/Profile
- game scope
- expiry/session-onlyかpersistentか

を表示する。

警告を毎Action表示して操作不能にしない。
Profile保存時に明示確認し、実行中は目立つ状態表示を行う。

例:
```text
Safety profile: CUSTOM / RELAXED
Disabled:
  - semantic destructive-action evaluator
  - repeat-cycle guard

Execution Safety Kernel: ACTIVE
```

## Flow Composition連携
#432では:
- LOCKED KernelはFlow graphへ置かない
- GUARDED nodeはdisable可能だがwarning metadataを持つ
- OPTIONAL nodeは自由にadd/remove/reorder可能

これによりFlowの自由度と最低containmentを分離する。

## Custom Script / Plugin
Script/PluginがActionを提案しても必ずKernelへ入る。

Pluginに:
- raw SendInput
- unrestricted PostMessage
- direct OS input bypass
を通常Capabilityとして与えない。

どうしてもOS integration pluginが必要な場合も、Executor adapter契約として別trust boundary/署名/開発用途に限定し、通常Flow Hookとは分離する。

## Benchmark / Test
Kernelは常時有効。

GUARDED/OPTIONALはtest profileでdisable可能。

これにより、
- pure model behavior benchmark
- full safety gameplay test
を分離できる。

## 非対象
- 全Safety Policyを絶対削除不能にすること
- Expertユーザーの実験自由度を不要に制限すること
- anti-cheat回避
- OS sandbox本体

## 完了条件
- [ ] LOCKED/GUARDED/OPTIONAL分類contractがある
- [ ] Execution Safety KernelがFlow graph外のExecutor boundaryにある
- [ ] Emergency Stop/release/lease/target/freshness/structural validationをKernelで保証できる
- [ ] FlowからKernelをremove/bypassできない
- [ ] GUARDED SafetyをExpert warning付きでdisable/relaxできる
- [ ] override状態をProfile/Journalへ記録できる
- [ ] UIでKernel ACTIVEとrelaxed policyを区別して表示できる
- [ ] Kernel error時fail closed
- [ ] custom Hook/Script ActionもKernelを通る
- [ ] fixtureでSafety Policyを全disableしてもKernel invariantが維持される

## 関連Issue
- #22 Action Safety Evaluator
- #33 SafetyGuard
- #40 Fail-safe Runtime
- #43 Decision Verifier
- #58 MOD / Hook Parent
- #122 Threat Model
- #151 Processing Hook Runtime
- #206 Unknownness Action Policy
- #392 Click Target Resolver
- #402 Temporal Target Stabilizer
- #432 Expert Flow Composition

## 補足
Safety Requiredを「全部の保護機能をユーザーから奪えない」という意味にしない。

削除不能なのは、**誤ったAI/Plugin/FlowでもOS入力が対象外へ漏れたり、古いcommandを実行したり、入力を押しっぱなしにしたりしないための最小containment kernel**だけとする。


## Emergency Stop input origin
Emergency Stop hotkeyの実装正本は#435。

- Stopは予約key codeそのものではなく、user-origin inputとして検出する。
- Kadoka自身が送信したESC/F12等はEmergency Stopを発火させない。
- Emergency hotkeyは変更可能。
- default候補はphysical/user-origin ESC。
- physical-only識別に失敗してUNKNOWNとなる場合は安全側停止policyを選択可能。

KernelとしてLOCKEDなのはEmergency Stop経路の存在とrelease/stop保証であり、「Esc/F12という特定keyをAIが絶対送れないこと」ではない。


## 決定事項まとめ
Safety設計は以下で確定する。

### 1. LOCKED: Execution Safety Kernel
削除・disable・Flow bypass不可。

最低限:
- Emergency Stop経路そのもの
- held input TTL / release-all
- runtime lease / watchdog
- stale / duplicate / generation mismatch rejection
- target/session authorization boundary
- Action schema / range validation
- fail-closed

これらはFlow StageではなくExecutor boundaryに置く。

### 2. GUARDED: Expert override可能なSafety Policy
警告・Profile記録付きでdisable/relax可能。

例:
- semantic destructive-action評価
- repeat/no-progress guard
- configurable rate/burst guard
- target stability追加確認
- confidence threshold
- optional dangerous-key policy
- additional verifier / agreement requirement

### 3. OPTIONAL
自由にadd/remove/reorder可能。

例:
- Self-Check
- Unknownness補助
- extra verifier
- ensemble
- additional observation
- Brain Message
- optional OCR/VLM
- exploration補助

### Emergency Hotkey
KernelとしてLOCKEDなのは「ユーザーが確実に停止できる経路」であり、特定key codeの予約ではない。

- default hotkeyはuser-origin ESC候補
- hotkeyは変更可能
- self-injected ESC/F12はゲーム操作として利用可能
- physical/user-origin同一keyだけEmergency Stopとして扱う
- ESC/F12をEmergency Stop用途だからという理由だけでAI Action deny-listへ固定しない
- 実装正本は#435

### Expert freedom
Expert/Developerは脳側のFlowやGuarded Policyを大きく組み替えられるが、最終OS input containmentだけは残る。

目的は「ユーザーからSafety設定を奪う」ことではなく、custom model/script/pluginが壊れても対象外入力・stale command・入力押しっぱなし等へ波及しない最低限のヒューズを保持すること。

## 2026-10-27 実装単位への分割
**本IssueはParent / 元の要求・設計の正本として維持し、直接実装対象にしない。** すべての元の完了条件は保持し、子Issueが各成果物を検証後、本Parentの統合条件を確認する。#19のPriority LabelとMethod Fidelity・Deferred Issueの追跡ルールに従う。

### Implementation子Issue（推奨順）
1. #518 — [Safety] LOCKED/GUARDED/OPTIONAL分類とPolicy契約をVersion化（P1）
2. #519 — [Safety] Executor最終境界からExecution Safety Kernelを削除不能にする（P1）
3. #520 — [Safety] Expert用GUARDED Policy Overrideの期限・Scope・確認履歴を実装（P2）
4. #521 — [UI] Kernel常時ACTIVEとGuarded緩和状態をPlay/Inspectorへ表示（P2）

### 既存Issueと重複させない関連責務
#435 User-origin Emergency Hotkey、#432 Expert Flow、#139 Inspectorは既存Issueを正本とし、子Issueは新しいSafety境界とProfile投影だけを実装する。

items.title: CONTROL ROOM: agent commands, email issue intake, app parking and safety gates
items.body:
# RESONATE Control Room — coordination contract (24 October 2026)

**Status: OPERATING PROTOCOL / INTAKE; NOT engineering approval.** This issue is a public, non-sensitive index of decisions, controls, and incoming findings. It does **not** grant any agent elevated runtime privileges. All work stays governed by Chas's explicit decisions.

## Authoritative lanes and owners
| Lane | Owner | Scope | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Captain / final sign-off | Chas | Vision, priorities, acceptance, spending, accounts, merges/releases | Final decision reserved to Chas |
| Conductor / coordination | Si Aye | Consolidate instructions, risk/terms/access review, evidence-backed handovers, status | No automatic cross-chat synchronization or hidden control over other AI apps |
| Code delivery / UAT | Cousin Dev | [#7](https://github.com/charlestdainslie-arch/Resonate/issues/7), current approved scope, three QA passes, fix defects | No blind merges, automatic vendor enrolment, production launch or self-approval |
| Independent integrity checker | Conductor / read-only helper | [#10](https://github.com/charlestdainslie-arch/Resonate/issues/10) baseline and regression check | Findings only; no code edits without separate approval |
| Future scope | Backlog | [#9](https://github.com/charlestdainslie-arch/Resonate/issues/9), Golden Thread/immersive motion, commercial model | Not a work order |
| Optional AI companions | Evaluation only | [#11](https://github.com/charlestdainslie-arch/Resonate/issues/11), individual free tools and isolated branches | No paid usage, write credentials or customer/private data |

## The standard commands — plain English instructions, not executable shell commands
- **STATUS** — return date, ticket, branch, SHA, deployment URL, what really works, what was not tested, blockers, next permitted action.
- **REVIEW** — read-only code, accessibility, interpretations, licence, privacy and user-visible copy review with cited evidence. Never modify software.
- **PROPOSE** — decision request with reason, benefits, alternatives, risks, costs, owner, impact; waits for Chas to approve.
- **SANDBOX** — only on an explicitly authorised isolated branch/copy; no production data or vendor-write credentials.
- **BLOCK / P1** — stop promotion if content is missing, a permission looks unsafe, a cost appears, or a quality gate fails.
- **ISSUE REPORT** — record symptom, reproducible steps, expected/actual, severity P0/P1/P2, branch+SHA+URL, screenshot/test evidence, privacy-safe remediation recommendation.
- **PARK** — remove a redundant helper from the *active workflow*, retaining its name, login link, purpose and reactivation checklist in the app inventory. Do not uninstall accounts, erase files or revoke access automatically.
- **REACTIVATE** — review free usage cap, data policies, permissions and duplication, then ask Chas for specific approval.
- **RELEASE REQUEST** — provide three-pass QA evidence, full features/copy inventory, before/after visual mobile/desktop UAT, regression status, and target exact commit. Chas decides; no self-release.

## Command precedence and scope
1. User's latest specific approval in context, with literal wording preserved.
2. Last exact approved code/UI baseline and dated evidence.
3. Active delivery issue #7 (fix work), P1 integrity issue #10 (blocker), evaluation issue #11 (read-only/non-prod), and future vision issue #9.
4. Ideas and exploratory chat are NOT blanket action authorisations. “Make it so, No. 1s” approves only the agreed scoped action; it does not override release, access or spending gates.

## Issue escalation by email
No direct email address or autonomous mailbox exists for the separate Cousin Dev chat. Until such a route is connected, prepare findings for Chas to send/forward using **subject: [RESONATE][DEV ISSUE][P0/P1/P2] short title** to his project Gmail. Include: issue number if available; owner; scope; reproducible steps; expected vs actual; links; branch; commit SHA; build/UAT evidence; any permissions/licence or privacy risk; proposed next decision. **Never paste passwords, API keys, private diary, health records or customer birth data** in project email or public GitHub. Si Aye can search the mailbox in a future interaction, but does not continuously monitor emails without an explicitly configured task.

## Companion registry and minimal-access policy
- **Operational connected surfaces for this project:** GitHub (issues/source), Vercel (preview/build evidence), Gmail (human-readable handovers), optional Drive files/dated backups.
- **Currently being evaluated** (not automatically signed in/connected): Antigravity, Copilot Free, Claude Free, Perplexity Free, Google AI Studio, Blender, optional Ollama; see #11 and verify current free limits.
- **PARK by default as least-essential extra agent:** Cline (duplicates Cousin Dev and may require paid model inference); retain for later, do not install/uninstall or grant access. Continue.dev remains deferred because of project maintenance concerns documented in #11.
- Reassess **every** added integration for: minimal OAuth scopes; read vs write rights; $0 plan/spend caps; trial auto-conversion; data retention/training; redistribution and commercial/software/model licences; secrets exposed to prompts/logs; source-code licensing; prompt-injection resistance; and supply-chain quality. Unknown = do not activate.

## Release safeguards
- Do not confuse Vercel READY or green CI with visually accepted behaviour.
- Preserve accurate Rider–Waite meanings, numbered gold spread positions, max two UNIQUE clarifiers, original contextual interpretation, Oracle flow, numerology/astrology only when validated, journal save→reopen and branded PDF fidelity.
- Audit all approved copy (including the opening and clarifier explanations) against exact last signed-off baseline; issue #10 stays open until evidenced resolved.
- Execute separate pass 1 functional/automated, pass 2 visual/accessibility/responsive, pass 3 independent end-to-end UAT, including error cases.
- Record any exceptions; return **PASS / FAIL / UNKNOWN** and a recommended next safe action.

## Minimal handover entry
```
Date and request:
Owner and authorization quote:
Scope, reason and issue:
Repo / base branch / working branch / exact SHA:
What changed (or not):
Evidence links / tests run (PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN):
Privacy, spend, terms and licence checks:
Regression blockers:
Next permitted action / Chas decision needed:
```

**Current state:** coordination documented only; no production source changes, merges, deployment promotions, app deletions, vendor logins, paid subscriptions or automatic monitoring authorised by this issue. Public repo: avoid sensitive information.

items.title: Do not silently ignore Vercel Agent stream overrides
items.body:
## Problem

`createKitaruToolLoopAgent(...).generate()` resolves and applies `KITARU_OVERRIDE` even when `KITARU_REPLAY_ID` is not set. The same agent's `stream()` method only checks for `KITARU_REPLAY_ID`, then delegates to a native `ToolLoopAgent` using the original settings.

As a result, a local model-swap check can use the replacement model through `generate()` but silently use the original model through `stream()`.

This is not a replay-safety hole. Replay specifications and policies require `KITARU_REPLAY_ID`, and `stream()` already rejects that case before execution. The problem is the silent inconsistency for the standalone override fallback.

## Reproduction

1. Create original and replacement language models.
2. Set `KITARU_OVERRIDE` to select the replacement model without setting `KITARU_REPLAY_ID`.
3. Configure the agent's allowed replay models and model resolver.
4. Call both `generate()` and `stream()`.

`generate()` calls the replacement model. `stream()` calls the original model without warning.

## Expected behavior

`stream()` must not silently ignore an active Kitaru override. It should either apply a supported and documented override behavior or reject the unsupported combination before a provider or tool call.

## Scope

This is a TypeScript Vercel AI adapter issue. The shared TypeScript replay resolver already exposes the override. No Python server, API, or worker change is expected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `stream()` no longer silently uses the original agent settings when `KITARU_OVERRIDE` is active.
- [ ] Any unsupported override combination fails before a provider request or tool side effect.
- [ ] `stream()` with `KITARU_REPLAY_ID` continues to fail closed before execution.
- [ ] Ordinary streaming without Kitaru replay or override environment variables keeps its native behavior and does not create a recording session.
- [ ] A regression test covers the standalone override case.

Related to #761. Found while reviewing the implementation merged in #768; #777 clarified the current documentation boundary.

items.title: ADR-0041: runtime safety controls — kill switch, agent circuit breaker, caps, throttles, mandatory approval — tracking
items.body:
Tracking issue for **ADR-0041 — Runtime safety controls** (Proposed, elitea-ng/elitea-docs#68). Implementation waits until the ADR is accepted.

- [ ] #1493 suspension model + kill switch that cancels in-flight runs, with a scheduled self-test
- [ ] agent circuit breaker: error rate, spend per hour, repeated tool failure, runs per hour; trips into an `agent` suspension that needs a human to resume (`resume_requires` by tier); scheduler job, off the request path
- [ ] per-run caps: `max_tool_calls`, `max_model_turns` (folds in `step_limit`), `max_spend`, `max_wall_seconds` (#1496), `max_records_read`. Hitting one ends the run with `cap_reached`; an audited `safety.override_cap`
- [ ] gateway throttles with `scope.agent_ids` / `scope.user_ids` in `internal/policy`
- [ ] tool categories (`read | write | delete | external_send | payment | code_execution`) declared in toolkit schemas; approval policy by tier × category that beats author settings
- [ ] #1491 always-on HITL decision ledger, mirrored to audit
- [ ] pipelines: nested pauses beyond one child level; the tier policy can require a `hitl` node on every path to `external_send`/`payment`, enforced at publish and at admission
- [ ] unattended runs: `on_approval_required: fail | skip | notify_and_wait` (never auto-approve); relates to #1434/#1435
- [ ] alert rules for breaker trips and suspensions in the chart

**Deliberately not built:** the business thresholds themselves (risk owners document them; they are linked from the registry); paging and on-call routing.


---

## Documentation (mandatory — this issue does not close without it)

Enterprises need clear, honest documentation of this control. The implementing PR updates the embedded docs (`apps/elitea-web/src/entries/docs`) and their nav in the same PR; UPGRADING or ADR text alone does not count. Hub and structure: #1502.

- [ ] **Pages:** `content/admin/enterprise-controls/runtime-safety.mdx` (breaker, caps, throttles, tool categories, approval policy, pipeline `hitl` requirement); `content/admin/budgets-and-governance.mdx`
- [ ] **What the control does**, for a security/risk reader: the risk it addresses, what is enforced, and what is not.
- [ ] **How to configure it**, for an operator: settings, defaults, permissions/roles, Helm values or env vars, and the admin UI path, with screenshots where there is UI.
- [ ] **Evidence:** which records or audit events it produces, where to find or export them, and an example event.
- [ ] **Customer responsibility:** what stays with the customer's own systems and how Elitea integrates with them. Linked from `shared-responsibility.mdx`.
- [ ] **Control catalogue row** in `content/admin/enterprise-controls/index.mdx` flipped to `Available` (or `Partial`, stating what is missing), linking the page.
- [ ] **Hardening checklist** entry in `content/deployment/` when the control has a setting a regulated deployment should turn on.
- [ ] Behaviour changes for existing installs (new defaults, refusals, migrations) in "What's new" and UPGRADING.
- [ ] Toolkit reference pages list each tool's category.
